5.0.0.en: The Amorites: Canaanite tribes, some of them east of the Jordan and some west of it.

5.0.2.en: Melted: their souls grew very weak because of their fear.

5.0.4.en: The Book of Deuteronomy. The kings of the Amorites west of the Jordan as far as the Mediterranean Sea heard of Joshua's defeat of Sihon king of the Amorites and Og king of Bashan east of the Jordan, and also of the Lord's drying up of the river Jordan before the people, and they were very afraid. And they remembered what happened to Pharaoh king of Egypt when he pursued the people after their departure and was drowned in the Red Sea, and so their fear increased. He mentioned the Amorites because they were the strongest of the Canaanite peoples dwelling in this region.

5.1.1.en: The children of Israel neglected circumcision in the wilderness of Sinai for 40 years, and the circumcised men who came out of Egypt had died in the wilderness. Therefore God admonished Joshua to make knives of hard flint stone to circumcise the males. Circumcision signifies Baptism, because in it a part of the flesh is cut off, which points to the nature inclined to evil, and the beginning of a new nature obedient to God. And because the sacrament of Baptism is the entrance to life in the Church, they performed circumcision before the war and the possession of the new land.

5.2.0.en: Foreskins: plural of foreskin, which is the extra skin that is cut off in circumcision.

5.2.1.en: The foreskins, a symbol of excessive, harmful desires, were removed and heaped upon one another; therefore they called this place "the hill of the foreskins", since the foreskins became a heap and they covered them with earth. In this way the circumcision of the people was accomplished as God commanded, and most likely those who circumcised the people were the priests and the Levites.

5.3.0.en: The men who came out of Egypt and were of the age for war had all been circumcised, but they died during the journey in the wilderness.

5.4.0.en: The wilderness: the wilderness of Sinai.

5.4.1.en: Flowing with milk and honey: it means the abundance of pastures in the new land, which makes the cattle give overflowing milk, and the abundance of crops and plants, which makes the bees' production of honey plentiful.

5.4.2.en: The men who came out of Egypt were circumcised, but they disobeyed God in the wilderness and refused to enter the Promised Land, so God swore that they would not enter the new land, full of good things, and they died in the wilderness. As for those born in the wilderness, they were not circumcised.

5.5.0.en: The Lord raised up the sons in the place of their fathers to fulfill His promise to them, and Joshua circumcised them as a sign of the renewal of the covenant with God.

5.6.0.en: They abode in their places until they were whole. This shows that a person's acceptance of the covenant with God is a joyful matter, but it calls for painful sufferings in striving, and the person must be patient and not move away from his covenant until God gives him victory over sin and healing from it (Lk 21:19), for "in your patience possess ye your souls". We notice that the fear of the peoples of the land of the Jews made them not attack them during the period of their pain after circumcision, as the sons of Jacob did to the people of Hamor and Shechem (Gen 34:25).

5.7.0.en: Sin is a burden that God rolls away, that is, takes down from our shoulders. The reproach of Egypt was the bondage of the Jews when they were in it, and then the mockery of the Egyptians toward them when they learned of their wandering in the wilderness for forty years without reaching the Promised Land. The place took its name from what happened in it.

5.7.1.en: How many of God's promises have we turned back from and not stood firm in, until God helps us by patience, prayer and striving, instead of our turning back and being defeated.

5.8.s.en: (2) The Passover and the ceasing of the manna

5.8.0.en: The plains of Jericho: the flat lands of Jericho.

5.8.1.en: After the circumcision of the people, it became permissible for them, according to the Law, to eat the Passover, because no stranger or uncircumcised person is allowed to eat of it (Ex 12:44-49). If circumcision signifies Baptism, as does the crossing of the river Jordan, then the Passover signifies partaking of the Body and Blood of the Lord, and Communion is not permitted except to one who has been baptized.

5.8.2.en: It is noticed that this is the third time the children of Israel ate the Passover: the first time was at their departure from the land of Egypt (Ex 12), and the second in the second year of their departure (Num 9:1-5). The Passover was supposed to be kept every year, but it was not kept except when they entered the Promised Land.

5.9.1.en: Parched corn: it is the wheat crop that is not fully ripe in the first of its season.

5.9.2.en: The people ate of the fruits of the Promised Land on the second day of the feast of the Passover, that is, the first of the week of unleavened bread, whether they had bought fruits from the merchants or found them as spoil in the houses of some Canaanites who fled for fear of the people. So they made unleavened cakes from the produce and fruits of the new land, and they ate unleavened bread because the Law prescribes eating unleavened bread for seven days after the feast of the Passover (Ex 12:15).

5.10.0.en: When the children of Israel began to get food from the Promised Land, there was no longer a need for the manna, and God cut it off, because a person ought to work with his hands and toil to obtain his need; but if he meets circumstances harder than his abilities, such as the barren wilderness of Sinai, God will intervene, even by a miracle like the miracle of the manna.

5.10.1.en: Be faithful in bearing your responsibility and in using all your abilities for the glory of God. God rejoices in your striving and will hold you accountable for your neglect in everything in your hands. And be reassured about the future, because if any afflictions meet you, God will intervene and solve them for you.

5.11.s.en: (3) Joshua and the captain of the host of the Lord

5.11.1.en: Joshua was occupied with the coming war with Jericho, especially since it was a fortified city; if it defeated him, his reputation in the land would be lost and his defeat afterward would be made easy, and he could not pass it by and fight inside the land for fear of falling into an ambush with the city behind his back. Nor could he retreat, since he and the people had crossed the Jordan and it had become a barrier behind them.

5.11.2.en: At that time God intervened and sent the chief of His angels, or appeared Himself, as some Fathers see it. God in His love appears to His children in the form that suits them: He appeared to Abraham in the form of three strange men who passed by his tent in the wilderness, and to Jacob in the form of an angel wrestling with him and another time in the form of a multitude of angels to encourage him; and here, because Joshua was about to enter war, He appears to him in the form of a man of war holding a sword.

5.11.3.en: The Book of Deuteronomy. The faith and courage of Joshua appear in his going toward the man holding the sword and his asking him whether he was with us or against us.

5.12.0.en: The man who appeared in the vision declared that he was the captain of the host of the Lord. The host of the Lord means the angels or the human believers in God, and what is meant by the captain of the host of the Lord is God Himself, because He accepted that Joshua worship Him, and He is also called the Lord Jehovah in. This worship is the worship of adoration and not merely respect.

5.13.1.en: The Lord repeated in Joshua's hearing what He had said before to Moses at the bush (Ex 3:5), to teach him:

5.13.2.en: 1- That the presence of the holy Lord had sanctified the whole place, for he was in the presence of the holy God.

5.13.3.en: 2- That Joshua is not the bridegroom of the Church or her kinsman, but her friend [see the law of the loosing of the shoe (Deut 25:9).] For Christ is the only Kinsman or Savior of His Church, and Joshua and all the prophets or priests who serve in both Testaments are instruments in the hand of God and not the Kinsman; therefore they take off their sandals when approaching holy places.

5.13.4.en: 3- That he might know that holiness, which is indicated by taking off the sandal made from the skin of a dead animal, is a life without which we shall not see the Lord (Heb 12:14).

5.13.5.en: God appears in your life, not only by visions but through the events of life, to encourage you, and you can feel Him if you seek Him from your heart, believe in His existence and are ready to obey Him; then He will make Himself known to you and guide you to live with Him.

6.0.0.en: Jericho: city of the moon, that is, the moon god, and the meaning of the name is also sweet fragrances, because of the spread of roses and sweet basil in its land; it is located 8 km west of the river Jordan and 30 km east of Jerusalem (Map 1). It is the town of Zacchaeus the tax collector and of blind Bartimaeus in the New Testament. Straitly shut up: tightly shut.

6.0.2.en: Jericho was the first city that the people faced in the Promised Land, and when its people saw the children of Israel in their tents opposite their city, after they had crossed the river Jordan, they shut the gates of their city tightly. The walls of Jericho were high and fortified, and perhaps watchmen were observing the movements of the children of Israel. All this shows how great the fear of the people of Jericho was of the children of Israel.

6.1.0.en: The Lord continues His speech with Joshua, affirming that they will take the city, and He uses the past tense to assure him of that victory over the city and all who are in it, however great their strength and might and however great the fortification of the city.

6.2.0.en: The Lord commanded the children of Israel to go around the city once each day for six days. The going around was of course at a sufficient distance for the circle to be wide, so as to include the very numerous people of the children of Israel, and so that they would be out of range of the arrows of the soldiers of Jericho on the walls. The people's going around the city has many benefits, the most important of which are:

6.2.1.en: 1- God's encouragement of the people and instilling a spirit of confidence and strength in their hearts to storm Jericho.

6.2.2.en: 2- Testing the people's obedience to God's commands so that they might obtain victory.

6.2.3.en: 3- Instilling a spirit of fear in the inhabitants of Jericho who see the children of Israel from the walls, and through their fear their defeat is made easy, and fear may lead some of them to repentance and belief in God.

6.2.4.en: 4- Teaching the children of Israel order and exactness in wars and in all their life.

6.2.5.en: The circle signifies eternity, so their going around Jericho signifies the necessity of thinking about and preparing for eternity so that a person may possess the Promised Land, which signifies the Kingdom of Heaven.

6.2.6.en: May you be obedient to God's commandments even if they seem to differ from your logic, and be confident that they are higher than your mind. Victory over Satan is by taking refuge in God and not by a person's confronting him relying on his own strength; as long as you hold fast to God, the power of Satan will collapse before you.

6.3.0.en: Trumpets: made from rams' horns and used in religious celebrations, giving out a strong sound that all the people hear.

6.3.1.en: The shout: a prolonged sound issuing from the trumpet, a strong sound announcing victory.

6.3.2.en: The ark of the covenant of God goes around in the procession around Jericho, preceded by seven priests with trumpets of shouting, which they blow on the seventh day after going around the city seven times, to proclaim the power of God and His victory over the wicked inhabitants of Jericho. Of course a number of priests, most likely four, were carrying the ark. The going around of the ark proclaims the presence of God in the midst of His people, who will give them victory over the enemies.

6.3.3.en: The people's going around for seven successive days implies that they went around on the Sabbath day as well. This is not a breaking of the Lord's commandment to sanctify the Sabbath day, because religious work or service is done on the Sabbath day, and it is not as the elders of the Jews thought, that no work is done on the Sabbath day, so that they opposed Christ for His healing of the sick (Mt 12:8). On the seventh day they go around seven times, and by this their strength is worn out, and then they blow the trumpets of shouting and shout, that is, it is God's power that will give them victory, and not their material strength or their weapons.

6.3.4.en: The going around for seven days, or seven times on the seventh day, signifies the work of the Holy Spirit in the seven sacraments in the Church, that is, that the people are subject to the Spirit of God, who will give them victory over the enemies.

6.4.0.en: God announced to them that after their going around Jericho seven times on the seventh day, and the priests' blowing of the trumpets of shouting and then the shout of all the people, the great walls of Jericho would fall, and then He commands them that every soldier is to rush upon the city wall that has collapsed before him, cross it and enter the city; that is, the circle of soldiers surrounding the city closes in on the city and storms it, killing those in it.

6.4.1.en: It is understood from this that the soldiers of war were in a circle around the city, and behind the soldiers within the circle was the ark of the covenant, with the priests carrying the trumpets before it; that is, the ark of the covenant was part of the circle, with the soldiers before it and behind it. The soldiers behind the ark He calls "the rereward", that is, the rear of the army.

6.5.0.en: Armed: the soldier prepared for war.

6.5.1.en: The rereward: the rear of the army.

6.5.2.en: Joshua carried out all that the Lord commanded, and the soldiers walked in a circle around the city, with the ark behind them and the bearers of the trumpets before it, and the rear of the army behind the ark; that is, the ark and the priests were between the soldiers before it and behind it. They blew the trumpet in intermittent blasts that frightened the enemies and encouraged the people of God. This is different from the continuous, strong blowing of the shouting which they did at the end of the going around on the seventh day.

6.6.0.en: Joshua commanded the people to walk in the procession around Jericho in silence, with nothing heard but the intermittent sound of the trumpets, and by this the people's obedience appears, their faith is strengthened, and they frighten their enemies, as we mentioned.

6.6.1.en: If we, the children of the Church, obey her teachings, our faith is strengthened and we frighten the demons; and by this we await God's victory. And as the people of God stormed Jericho, so also we triumph over Satan and set out for the Kingdom.

6.7.0.en: Joshua carried out God's commands and the procession went around the city, made up of the ark of the covenant carried by the priests, with the trumpeting priests before it and the soldiers before it and behind it; then they rested, and they did so on the second and third day until the sixth.

6.7.1.en: This procession was strange to the inhabitants of Jericho and the inhabitants of the neighboring lands, so some marveled, others mocked, and the rest were afraid.

6.7.2.en: It is noticed that Joshua rose early, as an active leader who carries out God's commands and leads his people with zeal.

6.8.s.en: (2) The fall of the city and its being devoted to destruction

6.8.0.en: All the people rose early on the seventh day to go around the city of Jericho seven times, and perhaps they walked faster so that there would be time for the seven circuits.

6.9.0.en: After going around seven times on the seventh day, the priests blew the trumpets with a continuous, strong blast, and Joshua commanded the people to shout the shout of victory because God had given them the city of Jericho, although their seizure of the city had not yet taken place, but Joshua speaks in the past tense because of his faith in the promises of God. The sound of the trumpets and the shout of the people stirred great fear in the hearts of the inhabitants of Jericho.

6.10.0.en: Accursed to the Lord: devoted to Him, and it is not permissible for anyone to take any of it for himself.

6.10.1.en: Trouble it: bring evil upon it.

6.10.2.en: Joshua continued his speech with the people and commanded them not to take anything for themselves from the possessions of Jericho, but that everything be devoted to God and that people and animals be killed, except Rahab and her household, because she believed in God and hid the two spies whom Joshua sent to Jericho (ch. 2). He warned them that none of them should take possessions from Jericho, lest he be punished by God and bring evil upon all the people.

6.10.3.en: God intended the killing of the inhabitants of Jericho because of their evils, and likewise the animals and all the beasts because they were used as sacrifices to the idols or some of them were worshipped; that is, God wanted to remove evil and everything connected with it, and to make His people exact in keeping away from everything connected with evil. When the idea was established in their hearts, He afterward permitted them, in some of their wars, to take the spoils, as in their war with Ai (ch. 8).

6.11.0.en: As for the metals of silver, gold, bronze and iron, they are holy to the Lord and are to be added to the treasury of the Tabernacle as the possessions of God.

6.12.0.en: The Lord fulfilled His promise of the falling of the wall when they shouted, and they took the city and carried out the Lord's command to devote its people and all its spoil. Here appears the effectiveness of the faith that made the people obey God in going around Jericho and not murmur like their fathers, so the walls fell by the hand of God and not by the hand of man, and every Jewish soldier rushed straight before him, that is, the soldiers stormed the city from every side and killed those in it, and the inhabitants of Jericho surrendered because of their great fear.

6.12.1.en: By faith you can obtain all your needs from God according to His will. So remember God's works and promises so that your faith is strengthened, and ask Him with confidence and obey His commandments, and you will live in joy.

6.13.0.en: The two spies entered the house of Rahab at Joshua's command and brought her out with all her household, but they did not join them to the people; rather they left them outside the camp until they were cleansed of their uncleanness.

6.13.1.en: It is noticed that the house of Rahab, which was in the wall of the city, did not fall and collapse, by the Lord's command, in order to save her; for God is able to save everyone who believes in Him.

6.13.2.en: Rahab was a cause of blessing for her whole household and clan, for she announced to them deliverance if they believed, and they obeyed her and believed like her, and she saved them from death and they lived with the people of God, and God rewarded her by her becoming the grandmother of David and of Christ (Mt 1:5). By this the first Gentile pagan woman from the land of Canaan, she and all her household, was joined to the people of God, and many joined afterward.

6.14.0.en: Even unto this day: until the day Joshua wrote this book.

6.14.1.en: The silver and gold were added to the treasury of the Tabernacle, and Rahab and all her household were saved and joined the Jewish people as a reward for her kindness to the two spies. We see from the genealogy of Christ (Mt 1:5) that Salmon son of Nahshon, the prince of the tribe of Judah, married her.

6.14.2.en: Do not grow weary in doing good, for Rahab did a kindness to the two spies, and the course of her whole life changed and she joined the faith and the holy people. Be confident that a cup of cold water will not lose its reward (Mt 10:42).

6.15.0.en: Joshua regarded Jericho as an accursed city because of its immersion in evils and idol worship, therefore the Lord cursed it and devoted it to destruction and ruin. And Joshua decreed that the curse would come upon whoever builds this city again, since he would be opposing God, who demolished it and overthrew its walls Himself. In fulfillment of the curse, whoever dares to do so, his children will all die: his firstborn will die when he lays its foundation, then their deaths will follow one after another until the youngest of them dies when he sets up its gates. This was fulfilled five hundred years later in the person of Hiel the Bethelite (1 Kgs 16:34). It is noticed that the talk here is about building Jericho as a fortified city, which God commanded to be demolished, but buildings were afterward erected beside the ruined Jericho and called by its name, and it is in these that Elijah and Elisha established a school for the sons of the prophets, and Elisha healed its main spring of water (2 Kgs 2). Christ Himself visited Jericho and healed the two blind men near it and visited the house of Zacchaeus in it (Mt 9:27, Lk 19).

6.16.0.en: The report of God's work with Joshua and His support of him spread through all the land of Canaan. Defeat before Ai
